zod-5917.text:
GOAL
Make optionality compose correctly through schemas whose input and output contracts differ.

OBSERVED MECHANISM
The reachable Zod 4 integration commit 85928549 established two directional facts: optin means an object/tuple may omit the input, while optout means the parsed output may be omitted/undefined. For a pipe, optin comes from the left/input schema and optout comes from the right/output schema. For optional(), both are optional. For default(), optin is optional but optout is not, because missing input materializes a defined value. Wrapper schemas propagate the appropriate directional flags.

BOUNDED IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE
The proven pipe pattern was:
  defineLazy(pipe._zod, "optin", () => def.in._zod.optin)
  defineLazy(pipe._zod, "optout", () => def.out._zod.optout)
Object input types use optin; object output types use optout. Commit 362eb330 then fixed an important execution edge: optional(inner) cannot blindly delegate merely because inner.optin is optional. When the original input is undefined, an error returned by the inner pipeline is cleared and the result becomes undefined. The sync and Promise paths use the same handleOptionalResult behavior.

PROVING EVIDENCE
The historical optional tests covered: optional before a pipe, optional after a transform, default before/after a pipe, object input/output type differences, and both normal and jitless object parsing. The regression test for 362eb330 used an optional property containing union -> transform -> pipe -> optional and required parse({}) and jitless parse({}) to agree. Inspect with: git show 85928549 -- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/optional.test.ts; git show 362eb330 -- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/optional.test.ts.

APPLICABILITY BOUNDARY
Do not infer that a schema is input-optional merely because it can emit undefined. Do not copy a special case for one wrapper position. Trace the current chain directionally and verify runtime parsing, inferred input/output types, and jitless behavior. Reject this episode if the current failure does not cross a wrapper boundary with different input/output optionality.

zod-5937.text:
GOAL
Keep absent-key handling, fallback materialization, inferred types, and generated JSON Schema consistent for wrappers with different input and output contracts.

OBSERVED MECHANISM
The historical work separated optin (may be absent in input) from optout (may be absent in output). Commit 57a1adf9 fixed object handling after proving that default/prefault accept missing input but produce a defined output: treating them like ordinary optional output silently drops fallback values. Commit 36fe14e1 recorded catch as input-optional and tested input-side JSON Schema required lists. Commit a7b1d18d later made the absent-key versus explicit-undefined distinction executable instead of treating every undefined-accepting schema as the same contract.

BOUNDED IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE
The proven directional facts were:
  optional(): optin optional, optout optional
  default()/prefault(): optin optional, optout required/defined
  pipe: optin from its input side, optout from its output side
  catch: missing input must reach the fallback path when its input contract permits it
Object parsing must run a schema on undefined when that schema can materialize a value. Omitting a key from the result is a separate output-shaping decision. JSON Schema's required array describes input requiredness and therefore follows optin, not optout.

PROVING EVIDENCE
Commit 57a1adf9 added nested default/prefault object cases for absent and explicit undefined inputs and asserted the actual output values. Commit 36fe14e1 added catch/union optionality and input JSON Schema assertions. Commit a7b1d18d added explicit absent-key versus explicit-undefined coverage. Inspect with: git show 57a1adf9 -- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/default.test.ts; git show 36fe14e1 -- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/optional.test.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/to-json-schema.test.ts; git show a7b1d18d -- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/optional.test.ts.

APPLICABILITY BOUNDARY
Do not solve this by globally marking every schema that accepts undefined as optional. Preserve the distinction among a missing property, an explicit undefined value, and a wrapper that replaces undefined with a defined fallback. Check both fast and jitless object paths plus generated input JSON Schema. Reject the episode if the current failure is unrelated to absent-key execution or directional optionality.

zod-5625.text:
GOAL
Expose one bidirectional transformation consistently across Zod's classic and mini APIs while preserving decode/encode types and composition.

OBSERVED MECHANISM
The reachable Zod 4.1 integration commit 019c370f implemented codec as a specialized pipe with an input schema, output schema, forward transform, and reverse transform. Classic and mini each expose their own constructor surface over the same directional core. Forward parsing validates the input side then transforms to the output side; backward encoding reverses that flow.

BOUNDED IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE
The classic factory constructs ZodCodec with type pipe, in, out, transform: decode, and reverseTransform: encode. The mini factory mirrors the public capability with its own constructor. Codec types preserve A as the decode input/encode output and B as the decode output/encode input. New compositional operations should derive a schema rather than mutate the existing codec.

PROVING EVIDENCE
The historical codec suite proves instanceof relationships, forward decode, backward encode, round trips, safe variants, async variants, refinements, nested composition, and static type inference in both classic and mini packages. Inspect with: git show 019c370f -- packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/mini/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/codec.test.ts packages/zod/src/v4/mini/tests/codec.test.ts.

APPLICABILITY BOUNDARY
Keep classic and mini API parity and preserve directional type inference. Do not mutate an existing codec or bypass the established constructor/factory pattern. Validate both runtime directions and compile-time input/output types.
